entities.summary: Mollie Steimer was an anarchist activist. A Ukrainian Jew, she left Russia and settled in New York City in 1913. She quickly became involved in the local anarchist movement and was caught up in the case of Abrams v. United States. Charged with sedition, she was eventually deported to Soviet Russia, where she met her lifelong partner Senya Fleshin and agitated for the rights of anarchist political prisoners in the country. For her activities, she and Fleshin were again deported to western Europe, where they spent time organising aid for exiles and political prisoners, and took part in the debates of the international anarchist movement.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Mollie Steimer's activism in the Abrams v. United States case and her subsequent deportations to Soviet Russia had a significant impact on the international anarchist movement, influencing the lives of political prisoners and shaping the trajectory of anarchist thought in the 20th century.
